nindian-history-1-4.s: Which script of Ashokan inscriptions was written from right to left and used only in the north-west?
nindian-history-1-4.x: Kharosthi, written right to left, was used in the north-west, as at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra; most Ashokan inscriptions are in Brahmi.

n866a206b55d.s: Erragudi (Yerragudi), the Ashokan edict site, is now in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
n866a206b55d.x: Erragudi lies in the present Nandyal district; it was earlier part of Kurnool district.

n1f109527723.s: Which of the following was promoted as a virtue in Ashoka's Dhamma?
n1f109527723.x: Dhamma promoted kindness and charity; cruelty, anger, pride and jealousy were condemned as vices.

na27c0cd1f86.s: After the Kalinga War, which policy replaced military conquest for Ashoka?
na27c0cd1f86.x: After Kalinga Ashoka waged no more wars of conquest; Dhammavijaya (conquest by Dhamma) replaced military conquest.

ne02326227fe.s: Which was the largest settlement unit in the Arthashastra, consisting of 800 villages?
ne02326227fe.x: Sthaniya had 800 villages; Dronamukha had 400, Kharvatika 200 and Sangrahana 10.

n027291ba8c9.s: Sita (crown) land in the Mauryan period was cultivated by:
n027291ba8c9.x: Sita land was farmed for the state using slaves and hired labourers, not exclusively by free peasants.

n51b7998e6e9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mauryan economy?
o: Good roads and state incentives encouraged crafts
Shrenis financed early Buddhist centres, including in Andhra
The state took a road tax from trade caravans
Mauryan coins bore portraits of the emperor
n51b7998e6e9.x: Mauryan punch-marked silver coins carried symbols but no portraits; the other three statements are correct.

n8b42130d836.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Mauryan trade routes?
o: Dakshinapatha was the great southern trade route
Dakshinapatha was the northern highway from Taxila to Tamralipti
The Krishna–Godavari delta was a node of Dakshinapatha
Uttarapatha ran from Taxila through Pataliputra to Tamralipti
n8b42130d836.x: The Taxila–Tamralipti highway was Uttarapatha; Dakshinapatha was the southern route with the Krishna–Godavari delta as a node.

nd63bff8532a.s: In a Mauryan pillar, which component sits directly on top of the shaft?
nd63bff8532a.x: The order is shaft, bell-shaped inverted lotus, abacus and animal capital; Mauryan pillars have no base.

n31d34b8f905.s: The Mauryan bull capital was found at:
n31d34b8f905.x: The bull capital is from Rampurva; Sankisa has the elephant, Lauriya Nandangarh the single lion and Sarnath the four lions.

new.s: In which year did James Prinsep decipher the Brahmi script?
new.x: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837.

new.s: The Maski edict, which proved that Devanampiya Piyadasi was Ashoka, was found in:
new.x: The Maski Minor Rock Edict, naming Ashoka, was found in 1915.

new.s: Ashoka is called 'Dharmasoka' in which inscription?
new.x: The Sarnath inscription calls him Dharmasoka; Maski calls him Buddhashakya and Bhabru 'Piyadasi Raja'.

new.s: The form of Ashoka's edicts, including the word 'lipi/dipi', follows the inscriptions of which Persian king?
new.x: Ashoka's edict form, moving from third to first person and using 'lipi/dipi', follows Darius's inscriptions.

new.s: The bilingual Greek-Aramaic edict of Ashoka was found at:
new.x: The Greek-Aramaic bilingual edict is at Kandahar (Shar-i-Kuna); Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra are Kharosthi sites.

new.s: The Kharosthi script is derived from:
new.x: Kharosthi derives from the Aramaic script of the Achaemenid Persians.

new.s: Ashokan edicts in the Aramaic script were found at:
new.x: Aramaic edicts come from Taxila, Laghman and Kandahar; Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra are Kharosthi, Girnar Brahmi.

new.s: How many Major Rock Edicts did Ashoka issue?
new.x: Ashoka issued 14 Major Rock Edicts, found complete at sites like Girnar and Kalsi.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an Ashokan edict site?
new.x: Besnagar (Vidisha) has the Heliodorus (Garuda) Pillar of the Bhagavata religion, not an Ashokan edict.

new.s: Sopara, a Major Rock Edict site of Ashoka, is in present-day:
new.x: Sopara is in Palghar/Thane, Maharashtra.

new.s: Which Major Rock Edict records the appointment of Dhamma Mahamattas?
new.x: RE V records the appointment of Dhamma Mahamattas, 13 years after consecration.

new.s: Five-yearly (quinquennial) tours of officials were ordered in which Major Rock Edict?
new.x: RE III orders quinquennial tours of officials.

new.s: Ashoka's Dhammayatras, which replaced royal pleasure tours, began with a visit to:
new.x: RE VIII says Dhammayatras replaced pleasure tours, the first being to Bodh Gaya.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Ashoka's Dhamma?
o: It condemned pride and jealousy as vices
It named the Four Noble Truths and Nibbana
Dhamma Mahamattas were appointed to spread it
new.x: Dhamma was a moral code, not Buddhist doctrine; no edict names the Four Noble Truths or Nibbana.

new.s: The Brahmagiri, Siddapura and Jatinga-Rameshwara Minor Rock Edicts are in which district of Karnataka?
new.x: These three Minor Rock Edict sites are in Chitradurga district; Maski is in Raichur, Gavimath in Koppal.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an Ashokan edict site?
new.x: Bhattiprolu is a distractor; Erragudi, Rajula Mandagiri and Maski carry Ashokan edicts.

new.s: Which Ashokan pillar later carried Samudragupta's prashasti?
new.x: The Allahabad-Kosam pillar, with PE I–VI and the Queen's edict, later bore Samudragupta's prashasti.

new.s: The Kosam (Kaushambi) pillar is traditionally said to have been moved to the Allahabad fort by:
new.x: Tradition credits Akbar with moving the Kosam pillar; Jahangir only added his inscription.

new.s: Which Pillar Edict gave Rajukas independent judicial power and a 3-day respite to condemned prisoners?
new.x: PE IV (26th year) gave Rajukas judicial power and a 3-day respite to the condemned.

new.s: In which regnal year of Ashoka was the Kalinga War fought?
new.x: The Kalinga War (261 BC) was in Ashoka's 8th regnal year; the 20th year is the Lumbini visit.

new.s: According to Rock Edict XIII, about how many people were killed in the Kalinga War?
new.x: RE XIII says about 1,00,000 were killed and 1,50,000 taken captive.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kalinga War:
1. It was fought in 261 BC.
2. Its cause was Kalinga's control of east-coast land and sea routes.
3. Rock Edict XIII describing it is included in the Separate Kalinga Edicts at Dhauli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; at Dhauli and Jaugada the Separate Kalinga Edicts replace RE XI–XIII, so RE XIII is omitted there.

new.s: Ashoka's son Mahinda led the Buddhist mission to:
new.x: Mahinda, later joined by Sanghamitta, went to Sri Lanka under king Devanampiya Tissa.

new.s: Which pair of Buddhist missionary and region is correctly matched?
new.x: Majjhantika went to Kashmir and Gandhara; Mahadeva went to Mahisamandala, Sona and Uttara to Suvarnabhumi and Rakkhita to Vanavasi.

new.s: In Kautilya's Saptanga theory, which element is called 'the ear of the state'?
new.x: Mitra (ally), the seventh limb, is called the ear of the state.

new.s: Which element comes third in Kautilya's Saptanga order?
new.x: The order is Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda and Mitra.

new.s: Among Kautilya's tirthas, the Antapala was in charge of:
new.x: The Antapala was the frontier officer in charge of border forts.

new.s: Which Mauryan tirtha was in charge of prisons?
new.x: The Prashasta handled prisons; Dauvarika the palace gate, Nayaka the city guard and Paura the capital.

new.s: The Mauryan Sulkadhyaksha was in charge of:
new.x: The Sulkadhyaksha collected tolls and trade and service taxes.

new.s: Which Mauryan superintendent was in charge of crown-land agriculture?
new.x: The Sitadhyaksha supervised crown-land farming and collected sita.

new.s: The Panyadhyaksha in Mauryan administration supervised:
new.x: The Panyadhyaksha handled commerce; the Sulkadhyaksha took tolls and the Lavanadhyaksha handled salt.

new.s: In Mauryan administration, the Akshapataladhyaksha was the:
new.x: The Akshapataladhyaksha was the accountant-general in charge of currency and accounts offices.

new.s: Which pair of Mauryan superintendent and charge is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Kupyadhyaksha handled forest produce; mines were under the Akaradhyaksha.

new.s: Mauryan provinces were mainly governed by princes called:
new.x: Provinces were ruled by Kumaras (princes) or governors, helped by Mahamatras.

new.s: Ujjain was the capital of which Mauryan province?
new.x: Ujjain was the capital of Avantipatha; Taxila, Suvarnagiri and Tosali were the others.

new.s: In Mauryan local administration, the Sthanika was a:
o: Tax collector over a larger division
new.x: The Sthanika collected taxes over a larger division; the Gramika was village head and the Gopa an accountant.

new.s: Megasthenes' Agronomoi were officers in charge of:
o: Districts – roads, irrigation and land measurement
new.x: Agronomoi were district officers; Astynomoi were the city officers.

new.s: How many members made up Megasthenes' municipal board of Pataliputra?
new.x: Pataliputra had 30 members in 6 committees of 5 each.

new.s: The sixth municipal committee of Pataliputra described by Megasthenes dealt with:
new.x: The sixth committee collected a one-tenth tax on sales, not land revenue.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan army administration according to Megasthenes:
1. It was run by six boards of five members each.
2. The navy was one of its boards.
3. Chandragupta's army had 30,000 cavalry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: six boards of five, including the navy, and an army of 6,00,000 foot and 30,000 cavalry.

new.s: Stationary spies in the Mauryan espionage system were called:
new.x: Samstha spies were stationary; Sanchara spies, such as tikshna and rasada, were wandering.

new.s: Which of the following was a wandering (sanchara) spy in the Mauryan system?
new.x: Parivrajika (women) were wandering spies; kapatika, grihapatika and vaidehaka were stationary (samstha).

new.s: The Mauryan kantakashodhana courts were presided over by:
new.x: Kantakashodhana (criminal) courts had three pradeshtris; dharmasthiya (civil) courts had three dharmasthas.

new.s: In the Mauryan revenue system, Pindakara was a tax on:
new.x: Pindakara was levied on groups of villages; vivita was pasture dues, vana forests and setu gardens.

new.s: Which Mauryan tax was paid only in cash?
new.x: Hiranya was a cash-only tax; Pranaya was the emergency tax.

new.s: Vivita in the Mauryan revenue system meant dues from:
new.x: Vivita was pasture land dues; sita came from crown land.

new.s: According to Megasthenes, the penalty for evading sales tax was:
new.x: Megasthenes records death as the penalty for evading sales tax.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mauryan revenue system:
1. Pranaya was an emergency tax.
2. Bhaga was normally one-sixth of the produce.
3. Bali was the income from crown land.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; income from crown land was sita, while bali was an additional levy.

new.s: In the Mauryan period, rainfall was measured near granaries in a unit called:
new.x: Rainfall was measured in drona; pana, mashaka and kakani were coins.

new.s: Which pair of Mauryan coin and metal is correctly matched?
new.x: Mashaka and kakani were copper, pana silver and suvarna gold.

new.s: The Mauryan copper coin Kakani was worth:
new.x: The Kakani was a copper coin worth 1/4 mashaka.

new.s: The main port of the Ganga basin in the Mauryan period was:
new.x: Tamralipti on the east coast was the main port of the Ganga basin.

new.s: Bharukachchha (Broach) was a Mauryan port on the:
new.x: Bharukachchha and Sopara were west-coast ports; Berenice was on the Red Sea.

new.s: Megasthenes came to Chandragupta's court as the envoy of:
new.x: Megasthenes was the Greek envoy of Seleucus and wrote the Indica.

new.s: In the Arthashastra, unpaid forced labour was called:
new.x: Vishti was unpaid forced labour (Telugu Vetti); karmakara was wage labour.

new.s: According to the Arthashastra, which of the following could NOT be made a slave?
o: A person punished by a court
new.x: Slaves came through birth, sale, war capture or judicial punishment, but no Arya could be made a slave.

new.s: In the Arthashastra, the term 'Moksha' means:
new.x: Moksha meant divorce; stridhana was a woman's property and vishti forced labour.

new.s: Learned men in Mauryan society were called:
new.x: Sishtas were learned men; Antyavasayins were the five mixed castes outside Aryan society.

new.s: Which Mauryan ruler followed Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola?
new.x: Chandragupta, a follower of Jainism, went with Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola.

new.s: Which Ashokan edict names the Ajivikas and Nirgranthas separately?
new.x: PE VII names the Ajivikas and Nirgranthas (Jainas) separately.

new.s: The 80-pillared hall of Mauryan Pataliputra was found at:
new.x: Kumrahar yielded the 80-pillared hall; Bulandibagh yielded the wooden palisade.

new.s: The Mauryan remains of Pataliputra were excavated by:
new.x: D.B. Spooner excavated Mauryan Pataliputra.

new.s: The shafts of Mauryan pillars were made of:
new.x: Mauryan pillars are monolithic shafts of Chunar sandstone with the Mauryan polish.

new.s: Which feature of Mauryan pillars marks them out from Achaemenid (Persian) pillars?
new.x: Polish, animal capitals and the 'lipi' idiom are Achaemenid similarities; the absence of a base is a Mauryan difference.

new.s: Which pair of folk sculpture and findspot is correctly matched?
new.x: A Yakshi comes from Besnagar; the chauri-bearer is from Didarganj, Manibhadra from Parkham and the nude torso from Lohanipur.

new.s: The Mauryan rock-cut elephant at Dhauli is near which river?
new.x: The Dhauli elephant stands by the Daya river near Bhubaneswar.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a Mauryan work of art?
new.x: The Kanaganahalli slab is Satavahana-era; Dhauli, Didarganj and Kumrahar are all Mauryan.

new.s: The Bharhut stupa was discovered by:
new.x: Bharhut, a Sunga stupa of c. 150 BC, was found by Cunningham.

new.s: The present form of the Dhamek stupa at Sarnath belongs to which period?
new.x: The Dhamek stupa had an Ashokan original, but its present form is Gupta.

new.s: Which is the oldest stupa of Andhra?
new.x: Bhattiprolu is Andhra's oldest stupa.

new.s: Which is the largest cave of the Nagarjuni group?
new.x: Gopika is the largest of the three Nagarjuni caves; Lomas Rishi is in the Barabar hills.

new.s: The Barabar caves are cut into:
new.x: The Barabar caves are cut into granite with a mirror polish.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nagarjuni caves:
1. They are in Bihar.
2. Their inscriptions belong to the 6th century CE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Nagarjuni caves are in Jehanabad, Bihar; their inscriptions are 3rd century BCE, not 6th century.
